title: saturation-aware-reservation-recycler-and-reservation-slack-metric
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers with bursty, low-duty-cycle workloads were reporting sustained over-reservation of Dedicated capacity. Over-reservation increases unit cost and causes oscillation when autoscalers attempt to reclaim capacity aggressively, which in turn triggers temporary SLA lapses. This PR introduces a saturation-aware reservation recycler (SAR) that: 1) tracks per-reservation headroom and a time-decayed utilization score, 2) exposes a new reservation_slack percentile metric to give operators visibility, and 3) performs conservative, staged reclamation of underutilized reservations to the shared pool to reduce waste without causing churn.

What this changes (summary): added a controller component that re-evaluates reservations against a saturation budget and a hysteresis window; new telemetry hooks and metrics; small autoscaler integration that factors in reservation_slack when deciding scale-downs; an operator-configurable reclaim_policy with modes: disabled|conservative|aggressive. Includes CLI/terraform toggle and docs updates.

Behavioral highlights: - Reservations with >70% of allocated slots idle for a rolling 30m are candidates; candidates are assigned a reclaim_score that decays over time and is gated by cluster-wide saturation signals. - Conservative mode performs a staged reclaim (10-25% of candidate capacity per cycle) and annotates reservations with reclaim_in_progress to avoid double work. - Aggressive mode can reclaim up to 100% of candidate capacity when cluster headroom is negative and sustained for N cycles. - Autoscaler uses reservation_slack_p50 and p90 to reduce reactive scale-ups when slack indicates reclaimed capacity will absorb bursts.

Migration and safety: default is disabled for current installations. For new Dedicated clusters the installer flips default to conservative. All reclaims are recorded as events and emitted to audit logs; there is an opt-out label for critical reservations. Unit and e2e tests cover controller invariants and reclaim rollbacks on failed provisioning.

Performance notes: in a controlled canary we reclaimed 18% of idle reserved capacity within 2 hours and reduced nightly scale-up churn by ~22% with no observable increase in p99 latency for active tenants.

Related work: follows on ENG-4321 (utilization-sampler improvements) and complements ENG-4387 (tenant-sla-feedback). Links: Linear ENG-4321, SUP ticket SUP-1298.

Files changed (high level): controllers/reservation/recycler.go, pkg/autoscaler/integrations/reservation_advisor.go, pkg/telemetry/reservation_metrics.go, docs/dedicated/reservation-reclaiming.md, deploy/terraform/dedicated.tfvars.example, test/e2e/reservation_recycler_test.go, charts/dedicated/values.yaml.

Operator config knobs: reclaim_policy, reclaim_cycle_seconds, reclaim_batch_fraction, min_reservation_idle_seconds, reservation_slack_thresholds (p50/p90).

This PR is intended to reduce dedicated idle spend and stabilize autoscaler oscillation without requiring manual operator intervention.

b4d2e18: add reservation_slack telemetry and percentiles, wire to metrics pipeline
c7e8f90: autoscaler integration — consult reservation_slack in scale-down decisions
d2f425a: docs, terraform toggle, tests and e2e coverage
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall this looks promising. Two things: ensure reclaim decisions are idempotent across controller restarts; add a metric for reclaim_rollbacks.
Maya Chen (author): Added idempotency by marking reservations with reclaim_in_progress and added reclaim_rollbacks counter (see reservation_metrics.go).
Lucas Rivera: Suggest limiting aggressive mode to clusters with >= 3 hosts to avoid single-host thrash. Added a precondition check in recycler.go.
Priya Desai: Please call out any tenants that might be affected by default conservative policy change in release notes — ops teams will want a heads up.
Nora Kim (SRE): CI flaked on one e2e initially due to test timing; reran and it passed. Verified no increase in 99th-percentile tail during canary.
release_notes: Introduce a saturation-aware reservation recycler (opt-in by default) which reclaims underutilized Dedicated reservations conservatively, adds reservation_slack metrics (p50/p90), and integrates with autoscaler decisions to reduce oscillation and idle spend. Admin knobs provided for policy tuning.
notes_for_ops: Default off for existing clusters. To enable: set charts.dedicated.values.reclaim_policy=conservative and tune reclaim_cycle_seconds. Monitor reservation_slack_p90 and reclaim_rollbacks. Use opt-out label 'dedicated.reclaim=disabled' for critical reservations.
risk_assessment: low-medium: reclamation is staged and auditable; full aggressive reclaim must be explicitly enabled. Tested in canary clusters and covered by e2e rollback logic.
